To find out where you are, open the Maps tab: it shows your position on the map as soon as your phone\'s location is on.
I can\'t tell you your address here yet, but the Maps tab shows your current position. Check that your phone\'s location is turned on.
Want to get your bearings? Turn on your phone\'s location and tap Maps. There you can see where you are and search for a destination from there.
In a new place, the Maps tab is a good companion: it marks your position and helps you choose where to go. Just remember to allow location access.
Let\'s take it step by step: first check that location is enabled, then tap Maps. On the Home screen, the camera also describes by voice what is in front of you.

I don\'t want to give you a wrong forecast, so I\'d rather not guess. Check the updated forecast on your phone and take what you need: umbrella, coat or water.
Safety tip: on rainy days the ground gets slippery. Check the forecast on your phone before leaving and, if needed, take it slower.
Let\'s go! Open the Maps tab, type the destination in the Destination field and pick one of the suggestions. The app shows the route, the distance and the walking time.
To plot a path, use the Maps tab: choose the destination and check the distance and estimated time before you leave.
Planning ahead helps a lot: look at the route in the Maps tab calmly and, if you can, tell someone you trust where you are going.
In the Maps tab you can search for the address or place you want to visit. The route starts from your position, so keep your phone\'s location on.
If the place is new to you, look at the route in the Maps tab in advance and pay attention to sidewalks, crossings and obstacles along the way.
I don\'t have access to your calendar yet. But you can save reminders in the Notes card on the Home screen and check everything on the Notes board.
How about organizing your day? On the Home screen, tap the Notes card and write down what you can\'t forget. Then just look at the board.
I don\'t know your appointments, and that\'s okay: you can note them on Home. Write calmly and highlight what matters most.
A good idea is to list the day\'s tasks first thing in the morning. Use the Home notes and pick a color for each type of reminder.
I can help you get organized: think about what you need to do today, in what order, and record each item in the notes on the Home screen.
Your notes are on the Notes board, on the Home screen. Tap Home and scroll down to the board to see them.
I don\'t read notes aloud here in the chat yet, but you can find them on the Home screen, on the Notes board.
To create a new one, tap the Notes card on Home. To review earlier ones, look at the Notes board right below.
Looking for your notes? Go to the Home screen and swipe the board sideways: each note appears on a little colored card.
Your notes live on the Home screen, on the board. If you haven\'t written any yet, tap the Notes card to create the first one.
Of course! Tell me: do you need help finding your location, planning a route or organizing your day? I can point you the way inside the app.
I\'m here to help. On Home the camera describes by voice what is in front of you, and in the Maps tab you plan routes. Where would you like to start?
An important tip: before leaving, check that your phone\'s battery is good and that location is on. That way WeSee works better.
If you want to explore a new place, plan the route in the Maps tab and walk calmly. Any questions, come back here.
Take a deep breath and go at your own pace. Use the Home camera to hear what is ahead and the Maps tab to know where to go.

Demo text: this content is only an example and is not a final legal document.

WeSee is an accessibility app that helps people with low vision move around outdoors, using the phone camera, artificial intelligence and maps. There are two experiences: that of the person with low vision (PCD) and that of the guardian who follows them.
WeSee aims to offer support by voice and on-screen information so the person can get around with more independence, and so the guardian can follow them, with the person\'s own authorization.
Users are responsible for keeping their account data up to date, using the app safely and staying aware of their surroundings. The link between a person and a guardian must only happen with consent.

WeSee features, such as obstacle detection, voice descriptions, maps and routes, depend on the camera, internet, GPS and artificial intelligence models that can make mistakes or be unavailable. Routes and detections do not guarantee accessible sidewalks, safe crossings or the absence of obstacles. WeSee does not replace a white cane, a guide dog, mobility training or the user\'s own care.
Use WeSee as a complement. Do not rely only on it for safety decisions, such as crossing a street. Do not use the app to monitor people without their consent.
These terms may change. When they do, the latest version will be available on this page.
Demo text: this content is only an example. It does not state which security, storage or data deletion measures are in place.
This page shows, in general terms, how privacy may be handled in WeSee. The final version should describe precisely what the app actually does.

An app like WeSee may handle account data (such as the name, email and phone given at sign-up), the approximate location of the device, camera images used to identify obstacles, notes and preferences such as language and theme.
The information is used to identify the user, describe the surroundings, calculate routes and allow the follow-up authorized between the person and their guardian.

The goal is to handle data carefully and limit access to those who are authorized. This demo text does not describe specific security measures; they should be listed, accurately, in the final version.

The intention is for the person\'s information to be shared only with linked guardians, according to the permissions the person has given. Any other sharing, if it exists, should be described in the final version.
The final version should explain how users can access, correct or request deletion of their data. At the moment, the app does not offer account deletion in its interface.
The official contact channels will be provided in the final version of this document.
A quick guide to the features the app has today.
WeSee is an accessibility app for people with low vision. It uses the phone camera and artificial intelligence to describe by voice what is ahead, and it has maps and a support chat.
For people with low vision (PCD), who carry the phone close to the body, and for the guardians who follow them, each with their own experience in the app.

On the Home screen, the camera sends images for analysis and WeSee speaks what it identifies, such as people, vehicles and stairs, and warns when something is very close. It is an aid: it can make mistakes and does not replace your attention.
How can I use the map?

Open the Maps tab, allow location access, type the destination and tap Search. Choose a result to see the route, distance and time. The walking route only appears when the route server is enabled for it, and it does not guarantee accessible sidewalks or safe crossings.
How do I link a guardian?
See Profile > My guardians (on the person\'s account) or Profile > Linked people (on the guardian\'s account). There you can generate a code and enter it on the other account to create the link.
How do I change the language?
In Profile > Language, choose Português (Brasil) or English. The change applies right away to the whole app and to WeSee\'s voice.
How do I change the theme?
In Profile > Appearance, choose between Light and Dark mode. Your choice is saved.
Does WeSee replace a guide dog, a white cane or other mobility aids?
No. WeSee is a complement and does not replace a guide dog, a white cane, mobility training or your own care when getting around.
What should I do if a feature doesn\'t work?
Check your internet connection, the camera and location permissions, and that GPS is on. Then close and reopen the app. If it keeps happening, try again later.
Account deletion is not available in WeSee yet. No data has been deleted.
When this feature exists, you will be able to request deletion from here. In the meantime, you can sign out of your account at any time with Log out.
